text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today as U.S. crude oil prices dropped nearly 8% for the week following diplomatic talks between Iran and the U.S. at the United Nations. When oil prices weaken, exploration and production companies like ConocoPhillips see lower revenue on the barrels they pump—even though the company still produces the same volume, it gets paid less per unit. The stock is now down 7.3% over two weeks, tracking closely with the broader oil selloff.

The price pressure reflects shifting market expectations around Middle Eastern supply. Saudi Arabia is actually increasing crude exports despite infrastructure attacks, and Iran is signaling willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear negotiations. These developments suggest the market is pricing in less geopolitical risk to global oil supply than it was before, which removes one of the key supports for elevated oil prices that had been benefiting energy companies.
